name: Avery Quinn
title: Full-stack and AI engineer
tagline: I build AI features people can trust, and the tests that prove they work.
about: I'm Avery Quinn, a fictional full-stack and AI engineer created to demo Openfolio. In this story I've spent six years shipping web products, most recently AI assistants in healthcare, where being careful matters more than being clever. I like small teams, clear writing, and measuring things before arguing about them.
highlights: Led the patient intake assistant at Harborlight Health; it now pre-fills intake forms for 12 fictional clinics, and nurses edit about 1 in 5 answers instead of typing every one.
Built the evaluation suite that gates every intake-assistant release: 600 scripted conversations, run on each pull request.
Created Fieldnote, an offline-first field notebook used by a (fictional) university ecology lab.
Maintains Relay, a small open-source WebRTC toolkit in this demo universe.

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer, AI
experience.summary: Leads the patient intake assistant: speech and chat front end, retrieval over clinic policies, and the evaluation suite that decides what ships. Mentors two engineers.

experience.title: Software Engineer
experience.summary: Built real-time dashboards for coastal sensor networks with TypeScript, Python and PostgreSQL; cut page load time from 6 s to under 1 s.

projects.name: Harborlight intake assistant
projects.summary: An AI assistant that asks patients intake questions by voice or chat and drafts the form for a nurse to review. Grounded in each clinic's own policies; every release passes a 600-conversation evaluation suite.

projects.name: Fieldnote
projects.summary: An offline-first notebook for ecologists that syncs photos, GPS points and notes when a signal returns. Built with SvelteKit, IndexedDB and a small Go sync server.

projects.name: Relay
projects.summary: A tiny WebRTC toolkit for voice apps: signalling helpers, TURN credential rotation and a test harness for flaky networks.

awards: Best Developer Tool, Harbor City Hackathon 2021 (fictional), for Relay
